newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe M3 money supply rises 27.15 pct in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe M3 money supply rises 27.15 pct in Aug.

text.p: Zimbabwe's year-on-year broadly defined M3 money supply grew 27.15 percent in August after a rise of 40.64 percent in July, the Reserve Bank said.

* NOTE - The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe has revised its monetary data going back to December 1993 following the introduction of a new, standardised call report system for deposit banks and other financial institutions.
The central bank said the new system improved and clarified the classification and sectorisation of banks' monthly returns.

Under the new system, the stock of M1 from December 1993 onwards had been revised upwards, reflecting the inclusion of call deposits in commercial bank demand deposits. This re-classification resulted in a decline in commercial banks' under 30-day time deposits and therefore a decline in M2 in the same period.

The new system allowed for separation of merchant banks' time deposits into under 30-day and over 30-day time deposits. As a result of this distinction, merchant banks' under 30-day deposits were classified as a component of M2, while over 30-day deposits remained a component of M3.
Previously, all merchant banks' fixed deposits were classified as long-term deposits and were, therefore, only reflected in the final broad money aggregate, M3.
